He is the former deputy executive director of the [[NBA Players Association]]. He is the former president and commissioner of [[Big3]]. ==Early career== Mason lived in [[Silver Spring, Maryland]] where he attended primary school at Calvary Lutheran School. He first attended high school at [[Sidwell Friends School]] where he was named [[Most Valuable Player|MVP]] at the school as a freshman. He then transferred to [[Our Lady of Good Counsel High School (Montgomery County, Maryland)|Our Lady of Good Counsel High School]] for his sophomore, junior, and senior years. Mason led Good Counsel to their best basketball year ever, with 29 wins and a number 19 final ranking on the USA Today Super 25 list. At Good Counsel he scored a total of 1,426 points. He was named 1999 All-Metropolitan first team by ''[[The Washington Post]]'', All-Washington Catholic Athletic Conference (WCAC), and all-county by the ''Montgomery Journal'' newspaper. He was also named 1999 [[Powerade]] "Mr. Basketball", awarded to the best player in the Washington, D.C. area.{{Cite web |url=http://www.virginiasports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/roger_mason_57075.html |title=Roger Mason Bio |access-date=2014-02-22 |archive-date=2018-05-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180505091501/http://www.virginiasports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/roger_mason_57075.html |url-status=dead }} ==College career== Mason played collegiately at the [[University of Virginia]] (UVA). In 2001, he was named to the [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC) third team. Mason set a free throw percentage record in UVA history with 86.89 percent made (since passed by [[Malcolm Brogdon]]) and is currently fourth on the ACC's all-time list for free throw percentage.{{cite web |title=ACC Career Free Throw Percentage |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/conferences/acc/leaders/ft-pct-player-career.html |access-date=28 January 2020}} ==Professional career== ===NBA=== Mason was selected with the 31st overall pick by the [[Chicago Bulls]] in the [[2002 NBA draft]] after his junior year. On August 12, 2002, he signed a multi-year deal with the Bulls. On December 15, 2003, he was traded to the [[Toronto Raptors]] for [[Rick Brunson]]. On December 16, 2004, he was waived by the Raptors. In September 2006, he signed a one-year deal with the Washington Wizards. In September 2007, he re-signed with the Wizards on a one-year deal.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/wizards/news/mason_070924.html|title=Wizards Re-Sign Roger Mason Jr.|date=September 24, 2007|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|access-date=August 5, 2012}} His role significantly expanded during the season when [[Gilbert Arenas]] and [[Antonio Daniels]] were injured. He responded by putting up the best numbers in his NBA career. On July 11, 2008, Mason was signed to the San Antonio Spurs for a two-year $7.3 million contract.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs_sign_mason_080711.html|title=Spurs Sign Roger Mason Jr.|date=July 11, 2008|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|access-date=August 5, 2012}} On Christmas Day 2008, he made a buzzer-beating three-point shot to beat the [[Phoenix Suns]].[https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2008/07/09/AR2008070902297.html Wizards Lose Mason to Spurs, Sign First-Round Pick McGee] Mason would finish the season with career highs in points, rebounds, and assists per game and it was also his only time to play all 82 games of a season.{{Cite web|title=Roger Mason On September 27, 2013, Mason signed with the [[Miami Heat]].{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14354|title=Miami Heat sign Roger Mason Jr|work=InsideHoops.com|date=September 27, 2013|access-date=September 27, 2013}} On February 20, 2014, Mason was traded to the [[Sacramento Kings]] in exchange for a future conditional 2015 second-round pick.[http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-trade-roger-mason-jr HEAT Trade Roger Mason Jr.] He was later waived the same day.[http://www.hoopsrumors.com/2014/02/kings-roger-mason.html Kings Waive Roger Mason Jr.] ===International=== In January 2005, he signed with [[Olympiacos BC|Olympiacos]] of [[A1 Ethniki|Greece]] for the rest of the 2004–05 season. Later that year, he signed with [[Hapoel Jerusalem B.C.|Hapoel Jerusalem]] for the 2005–06 season, which got sponsored by billionaire [[Arkadi Gaydamak]] shortly before the season started. He quickly became a major player of the team and led it to the [[Uleb Cup]] semi-finals and to the Israeli League Finals. ===Big Three Commissioner=== Mason served as commissioner of the Big Three league in 2017 and was fired in March 2018, for "corrupt practices".{{Cite web | title=Roger Mason Jr. fired by Big3 for alleged corruption; Ice Cube to fill in as commissioner - The Washington Post |
